newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria LNG not looking for alternative gas buyer.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria LNG not looking for alternative gas buyer.

text.p: The chief executive of Nigeria's $4 billion liquefied natural gas project said on Monday the company was not looking for an alternative buyer for gas ordered under a contract cancelled by Italian state power firm Enel.

"We are not trying to sell to anyone else, although there has certainly been interest, as it is not up to us to take any initiative...We expect full redress under the terms of the contract, under which it is very clear that we will get full compensation," Theo Oerlemans told Reuters in an interview.

Enel in December linked its decision to scrap the contract for an annual 3.5 billion cubic metres of LNG to its abandonment for technical, economic and environmental reasons of its own project to build a terminal to receive the gas.
Arbitration between the two parties is underway.
Oerlemans said that informal discussions were also taking place with Enel on finding an alternative means of bringing the gas into Italy.

"In parallel with the arbitration we are holding informal discussions with Enel, to look for alternative ways of getting the gas into Italy, however the financial settlement is up to the arbitrators," he said.

Despite Enel's cancellation of its purchase contract, Oerlemans said the project, which should produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of LNG a year, had reached a level of 30 percent completion and that shareholders would soon be contacted with plans for possible future expansion.
Shell Gas BV is the technical leader in the LNG joint venture with state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp. The other partners are Elf Aquitaine and Italy's Agip.
